Every capture releases contacts and pauses; automatic approximately 3s live / 1.2s FIRE observation boundaries shorten waits. No human reaction-time or causal game-quality benefit inference.
Continuous held-burst rearming comfort, physical phones, Safari, audio, hardware performance and continuous enjoyment unassessed.

between_attempts_learning: HOLD ROUTE changes to HOLD APPROACH and HOLD TO RECOVER near receivers, so the same visible action area can finish recoveries.
Threat TURN cue helps reveal offscreen targets but needs a fresh view; capture metadata can lag the actual rendered heading during a turn.
Target-down and coil OFF feedback distinguish progress from firing. Reload interrupts firing; armor/open cues explain ammunition expenditure.
Second attempt sampled entry firing without tap aim, planning map, DASH in charge-warning context, Heart optic and active deck defense. No claim of causal improvement from scores or pauses.

helpful_moments.observation: Large FIRE pad and separated MOVE stick supported two-contact move/fire drag; target-down label gave clear confirmation.
Map route, selected receiver and cover legend made the facility layout understandable at 844x390.
Named recovery checkmarks and changing objective made mission progress clear.
Numbered coil health/OFF indicators and open timer explained boss progress.
Result screen separated assisted shots, tap aims, route/approach assists from accuracy and eliminations.

frustrating_moments.observation: Charge guard ended partially hidden behind cover after first shot; needed a new target selection. Small silhouette and cover made immediate result uncertain.
Waiting for reload while exposed cost shield; the narrow coil opening and armor cycle demanded attention alongside rear threats.
DASH produced clear cooldown/displacement but left a close wall/cover view, with no confirmed phase evade. This single use cannot establish steering comfort.
Rear warning and forward route compete for attention; shield fell while routing. Threat text is useful but covers part of the scene.

scores.scale: 0 unusable; 5 functional with substantial friction; 7 good with clear remaining friction; 9 excellent in assessed scope; 10 exceptional. Subjective holistic evaluation of these two synthetic paused mobile runs, not a win/loss grade or arithmetic average.

controls.reason: Large separated controls, tap aim, MOVE/FIRE drag, scene swipe and DASH all responded. Target acquisition near cover needed correction; unaided precision, continuous holds and real thumb ergonomics remain unassessed.

gameplay.reason: Recovery, patrols, armor openings and deck defense supplied distinct observed tasks with legible feedback. Assisted navigation reduced exploration burden and most of this review used it; short paused runs do not establish sustained enjoyment or challenge balance.

presentation.reason: Cohesive rainy station, teal/gold signals, illuminated machinery and restrained result screen convey a strong atmosphere in still captures. Audio and real-time hardware smoothness unassessed.

usability.reason: Context action labels, named checkmarks, threat TURN prompts, map route and explicit START FRESH made progression understandable without source knowledge. Facing/target changes require fresh orientation and many simultaneous cues compete.

readability.reason: Health/ammo, objectives and action pads are readable at 844x390; small distant guards, low-contrast gray geometry, compact compass/announcement text and overlapping world labels demand inspection.

unassessed: Recovered memory reading and unvisited optional content

method.screenshots: Every capture viewed separately before dependent adaptive input. At most one new scene target per batch; fresh view after turn. No keyboard/mouse/evaluation/internal handles.
method.boundaries: Waits at most 12000ms; first route request 12000 shortened to about 2985ms. Later route waits about 3000 shortened by boundary; inspected returned images/timings. No boundary bypass.
method.pause_lifecycle: Contacts released at captures and mission paused. Observation is much more frequent than continuous human play. No reaction-time or causal game-quality benefit inferred. Both capture modes break continuous holds; no captureHeld used. AIM/TOOLS not sampled.
